slides.text: Modern Chhattisgarh Industries Agriculture Irrigation and power Mineral resources Information technology Transport Tourist centers Chhattisgarh as the 26th State of the Union fulfills the long-cherished demand of the people. In 1904 Sambalpur was transferred to Odisha and the estates of Sarguja were transferred from Bengal to Chhattisgarh. Chhattisgarh is bounded by southern Jharkhand and Odisha in the east, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra in the west, Uttar Pradesh and western Jharkhand in the north, and Andhra Pradesh in the south.

slides.text: Area-wise Chhattisgarh is the ninth-largest State and population-wise it is the seventeenth state of the nation. Industries The economy of Chhattisgarh is largely natural resource-driven and it leverages the state ' s rich mineral resources. The key sectors where Chhattisgarh has a competitive advantage include cement, mining, steel, aluminum, and power.

slides.text: One of the most mineral-rich states in India, Chhattisgarh provides a lucrative opportunity for cement production at the most competitive prices. Agriculture Chhattisgarh has been dubbed "Dhaan ka Katora" ( Bowl of Rice ) of Central India, with the main crop being Paddy. Apart from paddy, cereals like maize, Kodo-K utki , and other smal l millets, pulses like tur and K ulthi , and oilseeds like Groundnut, Soybean, Niger , and Sunflower are also grown.

slides.text: Mineral Resources Chhattisgarh has the perfect geological set up to host several economically crucial minerals. Large deposits of coal, iron ore, limestone, bauxite, and dolomite are found in various parts of the state. Districts of North Chhattisgarh such as Surguja, Raigarh, Koriya, and Bilaspur are known for huge coal deposits.

E-Governance in Chhattisgarh is oriented towards ensuring people access to government.

slides.text: Tourist Centers Chhattisgarh situated in the heart of India is endowed with a rich cultural heritage and attractive natural diversity. The State is full of ancient monuments, rare wildlife species, carved temples, Buddhist sites, palaces, waterfalls, caves, rock paintings, and hill plateaus. Bastar, with its unique cultural and ecological identity; Chitrakote Falls, a spot where the river Indravati has an abrupt fall of 96 ft.; Tirathgarh Falls, the picturesque waterfall of Kanger river from a height of 100 ft. in the form of steps; Keshkal valley; Kanger Ghati National Park; Kailash caves; Sita Bongara and Kutumbsar caves are rich in natural beauty.

Even after a hundred years of Gandhi ' s visit to the Durg, the families of his followers say that even today there is a feeling of Gandhi ' s arrival at these places of the Durg.

slides.text: Gandhian Heritage in Mahasamund Gandhigram Tamora The movement known as "Tamora Jungle Satyagraha" took place at this place from 8 September to 24 September 1930. In this movement, nearby tribals actively participated in this movement. During the Satyagraha, when the police used force on the male protesters by the British, the women here took over the leadership of the movement.

slides.text: The British enacted the Forest Act and local residents were prohibited from entering the forest. Tamora's Satyagraha happened to break this law, was part of Gandhi's Civil disobedience movement, which started by Raghuvar Singh Dewan in Tamora. During this movement, Raghuvar Singh Dewan, a resident of Tamora, was sentenced to three months' imprisonment and a fine of Rs 200
